# Money tracking without the boring part

Say what you spent. Qalta writes it down and sorts it.

-   Voice
-   Scan
-   Private

[Download on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/id6756010294)

![Qalta Insights: 91% of income saved, a spending chart, spending trend, and daily average.](https://qalta.app/assets/home/hero-insights.webp) ![The Qalta Home screen: a net of $13,154 for this month, $14,400 income in green, $1,246 spent in orange, and transactions grouped by day.](https://qalta.app/assets/home/hero-home.webp) ![Adding an expense in Qalta: an empty amount, the Wallet account, today’s date, category icons, and a keypad.](https://qalta.app/assets/home/hero-add.webp)

## Just speak to log Add expenses in seconds

One sentence can become several rows, even a subscription and a transfer.

Receipts, bills, PDFs, CSVs, and bank statements.

## Track money together One budget for two or a family

Share a space with a partner, family, or roommates. Everyone adds expenses, and the totals stay the same on every phone.

![Three Qalta coin avatars, silver, gold, and bronze, floating above the clouds.](https://qalta.app/assets/home/shared.webp)

-   ### Invite with a link

    Up to 6 people in one space. Send a link, and they’re in.

-   ### Always in sync

    Accounts, budgets, and transactions update on every phone and on your other devices.

-   ### See who added what

    Each transaction shows who created it and who edited it last.

-   ### Private stays private

    Keep personal spaces on your iPhone. Only the space you share is uploaded.

## Questions and short answers

**What is Qalta?**

Qalta is an expense tracker and budget app for iPhone. You say what you spent or scan a receipt, and Qalta writes the transaction down and sorts it into a category. It also handles budgets, subscriptions, goals, debts, multiple currencies, and shared budgets.

**Can I share a budget with my partner or family?**

Yes. Create a shared space and invite people with a link. Up to 6 people can be in one space. Everyone sees and edits the same accounts, transactions, and budgets, changes sync automatically, and each transaction shows who created or last edited it. Shared spaces are part of Qalta Pro.

**How does voice expense tracking work?**

Tap the microphone and say something like “Coffee $5 and Netflix $10 every month”. Qalta fills in the amount, category, account, and repeat schedule. One sentence can hold several transactions, including transfers and subscriptions.

**Can Qalta log Apple Pay purchases automatically?**

Yes. A Shortcuts automation saves every Apple Pay payment with its amount and merchant. On iOS 27 a bank app’s payment notification can create an expense too. Follow the [step-by-step guides](https://qalta.app/tutorials/).

**Can I move my history from another budgeting app?**

Yes. Qalta imports CSV files from YNAB, Monarch, Copilot, Rocket Money, Spendee, Monefy, ZenMoney, CoinKeeper, and other apps, and exports your data to CSV at any time.

**Is my financial data private?**

A private space stays on your iPhone, with optional backup to your own iCloud. A shared space is uploaded only when you choose to share it, and only the people you invite can see it. Voice recordings and scans are sent to Qalta’s server and OpenAI only to read them. There are no ads.

**How much does Qalta cost?**

Qalta is free to download with a free plan. Qalta Pro adds unlimited transactions, voice, and scans, plus shared spaces, for $3.99 a month or $29.99 a year. The Family plan shares Pro with up to 6 people for $5.99 a month or $49.99 a year. Prices are in US dollars and vary by region.

**Which devices and languages does Qalta support?**

Qalta runs on iPhone with iOS 16.4 or later, and also on Macs with Apple silicon and Apple Vision Pro. It is available in English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Kazakh, Korean, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, Thai, Turkish, and Ukrainian.

![Qalta app icon](https://qalta.app/assets/home/icon.webp)

# Apple Pay automation on iOS 27

After an Apple Pay payment, Qalta can save the purchase as an expense. Amount and merchant come from the Wallet transaction; you can pick category and account each time, or set them in advance.

You need iOS 27, **Qalta** and **Shortcuts**, and cards in Wallet. On iOS 27 the Wallet trigger lives inside a new shortcut — there is no separate Automation tab.

1.  Open **Shortcuts** and tap the **+** button at the bottom to create a new shortcut.

    ![All Shortcuts with the plus button](https://qalta.app/assets/apple-pay-ios-27/en/01-shortcuts.png)
    *New shortcut*

2.  An empty editor opens. In the action search, tap the **Automation** chip — or type “Automation”.

    ![Empty shortcut editor with the Automation chip](https://qalta.app/assets/apple-pay-ios-27/en/02-new-shortcut.png)
    *Automation chip*

3.  Under **Apps**, tap **Wallet** — “When I tap a Wallet Card or Pass” (payment at a terminal).

    ![Wallet trigger in the Automation list](https://qalta.app/assets/apple-pay-ios-27/en/03-wallet-trigger.png)
    *Wallet trigger*

4.  The first block says **When Any Card is tapped**. If you only want Qalta to run for some cards, tap the blue **Any Card** chip.

    ![When Any Card is tapped trigger](https://qalta.app/assets/apple-pay-ios-27/en/04-any-card.png)
    *Any Card*

5.  Select the card you pay with (for example **Kaspi Gold**). Tap the checkmark.

    ![Selecting a payment card](https://qalta.app/assets/apple-pay-ios-27/en/05-select-card.png)
    *Which card to track*

6.  You should now see one block: **When \[your card\] is tapped**. In the search field at the bottom, type **Qalta**.

    ![Wallet trigger for the selected card](https://qalta.app/assets/apple-pay-ios-27/en/06-card-tapped.png)
    *Card trigger is set*

7.  Tap **Create Wallet Expense** (not “Create Transaction”).

    ![Searching for Create Wallet Expense](https://qalta.app/assets/apple-pay-ios-27/en/07-search-qalta.png)
    *Qalta action*

8.  You should see two blocks: the Wallet trigger and the Qalta action. Tap the gray **Amount** field — a keypad appears. Above it, tap **Select Variable**.

    ![Amount field and Select Variable](https://qalta.app/assets/apple-pay-ios-27/en/08-tap-amount.png)
    *Tap Amount, then Select Variable*

9.  On the Select Variable screen, tap the blue **Transaction** chip under the Wallet trigger. That is the Apple Pay payment, not Shortcut Input.

    ![Selecting Transaction from the Wallet trigger](https://qalta.app/assets/apple-pay-ios-27/en/09-select-transaction.png)
    *Transaction*

10.  Tap the blue **Transaction** chip that now sits inside the Qalta action. In the sheet, do not leave the checkmark on “Transaction” — tap **Amount**.

     ![Transaction properties: tap Amount](https://qalta.app/assets/apple-pay-ios-27/en/10-pick-amount.png)
     *Get → Amount*

11.  Repeat for the store name. Tap the chevron on the Qalta action to expand the fields. Tap **Merchant** → **Select Variable** → **Transaction**. Tap the chip again and pick **Merchant** from the list — not “Transaction”.

     ![Picking Merchant from the transaction](https://qalta.app/assets/apple-pay-ios-27/en/11-merchant.png)
     *Get → Merchant*

12.  The remaining fields are optional. Options for **Category** and **Account**:

     -   **Choose** — pick a specific category or account from Qalta. If you only have one account, do that: select it once. You do not need Ask Each Time.
     -   **Ask Each Time** — after each payment Qalta will ask where to save the expense. Useful if you have several categories or accounts.
     -   You can leave **Choose** empty — Qalta will use defaults and try to detect the category.

     **Currency**, **Note**, and **Date** can stay empty. Turn on **Show When Run** so a confirmation appears after payment. Tap the back arrow.

     ![Category, Account, and Show When Run](https://qalta.app/assets/apple-pay-ios-27/en/12-category-account.png)
     *Category, account, and confirmation*

13.  The shortcut appears under **All Shortcuts** as **Create Wallet Expense**. After your next Apple Pay purchase with the selected card, Qalta will offer to save the expense.

     ![Create Wallet Expense in All Shortcuts](https://qalta.app/assets/apple-pay-ios-27/en/13-all-shortcuts.png)
     *All set*

*Setup walkthrough on iOS 27.*

# Bank notification automation on iOS 27

When your bank app sends a payment notification, Qalta can save it as an expense. The amount and merchant are parsed from the notification text.

You need iOS 27, **Qalta** and **Shortcuts**, and a bank app that posts lock-screen notifications. This trigger is not available on iOS 26.

1.  Open **Shortcuts** and tap the **+** button at the bottom to create a new shortcut.

    ![All Shortcuts with the plus button](https://qalta.app/assets/push-notification-ios-27/en/01-shortcuts.png)
    *New shortcut*

2.  An empty editor opens. In the action search, tap the **Automation** chip — or type “Automation”.

    ![Empty shortcut editor with the Automation chip](https://qalta.app/assets/push-notification-ios-27/en/02-new-shortcut.png)
    *Automation chip*

3.  Under **Apps**, tap **Notification** — “When I receive a notification from …”.

    ![Notification trigger in the Automation list](https://qalta.app/assets/push-notification-ios-27/en/03-notification-trigger.png)
    *Notification trigger*

4.  The first block says **When I receive a notification from App**. Tap the blue **App** chip to choose your bank.

    ![When I receive a notification from App](https://qalta.app/assets/push-notification-ios-27/en/04-from-app.png)
    *Choose the app*

5.  Search for your bank and tap the app that sends payment alerts (for example **Kaspi.kz**, not a related Pay or QR app).

    ![App picker searching for the bank](https://qalta.app/assets/push-notification-ios-27/en/05-pick-bank.png)
    *Bank app*

6.  You should now see **When I receive a notification from \[bank\]**. In the search field at the bottom, type **Qalta**.

    ![Notification trigger for the selected bank app](https://qalta.app/assets/push-notification-ios-27/en/06-bank-selected.png)
    *Bank trigger is set*

7.  Tap **Log Bank Expense** (not “Create Wallet Expense” and not “Create Transaction”).

    ![Searching for Log Bank Expense](https://qalta.app/assets/push-notification-ios-27/en/07-search-qalta.png)
    *Qalta action*

8.  You should see two blocks: the notification trigger and **Log bank expense from Notification body**. Tap the gray **Notification body** field.

    ![Log bank expense with Notification body field](https://qalta.app/assets/push-notification-ios-27/en/08-tap-body.png)
    *Tap Notification body*

9.  A keyboard appears. Above it, tap **Select Variable**, then tap the blue **Notification** chip under the trigger.

    ![Select Variable with the Notification chip](https://qalta.app/assets/push-notification-ios-27/en/09-select-variable.png)
    *Select Variable → Notification*

10.  Tap the blue **Notification** chip that now sits inside the Qalta action. In the sheet, do not leave the checkmark on “Notification” — tap **Body**. Qalta reads the amount from the notification text, not from the whole notification object.

     ![Notification properties: tap Body](https://qalta.app/assets/push-notification-ios-27/en/10-pick-body.png)
     *Get → Body*

11.  The Qalta action should now say **Log bank expense from Body**.

     ![Body mapped into Log bank expense](https://qalta.app/assets/push-notification-ios-27/en/11-body-mapped.png)
     *Body is mapped*

12.  The remaining fields are optional. Tap the chevron to expand them. Options for **Category** and **Account**:

     -   **Choose** — pick a specific category or account from Qalta. If you only have one account, do that: select it once. You do not need Ask Each Time.
     -   **Ask Each Time** — after each notification Qalta will ask where to save the expense. Useful if you have several categories or accounts.
     -   You can leave **Choose** empty — Qalta will use defaults and try to detect the category.

     **Note** and **Date** can stay empty. Turn on **Show When Run** so a confirmation appears. Tap the back arrow.

     ![Category, Account, and Show When Run](https://qalta.app/assets/push-notification-ios-27/en/12-category-account.png)
     *Category, account, and confirmation*

13.  The shortcut appears under **All Shortcuts** as **Log Bank Expense**. After the next payment notification from that bank app, Qalta will offer to save the expense.

     ![Log Bank Expense in All Shortcuts](https://qalta.app/assets/push-notification-ios-27/en/13-all-shortcuts.png)
     *All set*

# Apple Pay automation on iOS 26

After an Apple Pay payment, Qalta can save the purchase as an expense. Amount and merchant come from the transaction; you can pick category and account each time, or set them in advance.

You need iOS 26, **Qalta** and **Shortcuts**, and cards in Wallet.

1.  Open **Settings → Wallet & Apple Pay**. Turn on **Live Activities** and **Cellular Data**.

    ![Wallet and Apple Pay permissions](https://qalta.app/assets/apple-pay-ios-26/en/01-wallet-settings.png)
    *Wallet permissions*

2.  Open **Shortcuts**, go to the **Automation** tab, and tap **New Automation**.

    ![Shortcuts Automation tab](https://qalta.app/assets/apple-pay-ios-26/en/02-automation-tab.png)
    *New automation*

3.  Choose **Wallet** — “When I tap a Wallet Card or Pass” (payment at a terminal).

    ![Wallet trigger in the automation list](https://qalta.app/assets/apple-pay-ios-26/en/03-wallet-trigger.png)
    *Wallet trigger*

4.  Select the cards you want Qalta to track. Tap **Next**.

    ![Selecting payment cards](https://qalta.app/assets/apple-pay-ios-26/en/04-select-cards.png)
    *Which cards to track*

5.  Keep the Wallet categories you care about (all is fine). Select **Run Immediately** (not Run After Confirmation). Tap **Next**.

    ![Wallet categories](https://qalta.app/assets/apple-pay-ios-26/en/05-categories.png)
    *Categories*

6.  On the tile screen, tap the gray **Create New Shortcut** card at the top left. Do not pick an existing shortcut from the list below.

    ![Create New Shortcut tile](https://qalta.app/assets/apple-pay-ios-26/en/06-create-shortcut.png)
    *New shortcut*

7.  An empty editor opens. In the action search at the bottom, type **Qalta** and tap **Create Wallet Expense** (not “Create Transaction”).

    ![Searching for Create Wallet Expense](https://qalta.app/assets/apple-pay-ios-26/en/07-search-qalta.png)
    *Qalta action*

8.  You should see two blocks: “Receive transaction as input” and the Qalta action. Tap the gray **Amount** field in the Qalta action — a keypad appears. Above it, tap **Select Variable**.

    ![Amount field and Select Variable](https://qalta.app/assets/apple-pay-ios-26/en/08-tap-amount.png)
    *Tap Amount, then Select Variable*

9.  On the Select Variable screen, tap the blue **Shortcut Input** chip under “Receive transaction as input”.

    ![Selecting Shortcut Input as the variable](https://qalta.app/assets/apple-pay-ios-26/en/09-select-variable.png)
    *Shortcut Input*

10.  Tap the blue **Shortcut Input** chip that now sits inside the Qalta action. In the sheet, Type should be **Transaction**. Do not leave the checkmark on “Transaction” — scroll the list and tap **Amount**.

     ![Transaction properties: tap Amount](https://qalta.app/assets/apple-pay-ios-26/en/10-pick-amount.png)
     *Type Transaction → Amount*

11.  Repeat for the store name. Tap the chevron on the Qalta action to expand the fields. Tap **Merchant** → **Select Variable** → **Shortcut Input**. Tap the chip again, Type **Transaction**, then pick **Merchant** from the list.

     ![Picking Merchant from the transaction](https://qalta.app/assets/apple-pay-ios-26/en/11-merchant.png)
     *Type Transaction → Merchant*

12.  The remaining fields are optional. Options for **Category** and **Account**:

     -   **Choose** — pick a specific category or account from Qalta. If you only have one account, do that: select it once. You do not need Ask Each Time.
     -   **Ask Each Time** — after each payment Qalta will ask where to save the expense. Useful if you have several categories or accounts.
     -   You can leave **Choose** empty — Qalta will use defaults and try to detect the category.

     **Currency**, **Note**, and **Date** can stay empty. Turn on **Show When Run** so a confirmation appears after payment. Tap the blue checkmark at the top.

     ![Category, Account, and Show When Run](https://qalta.app/assets/apple-pay-ios-26/en/12-category-account.png)
     *Category, account, and confirmation*

13.  The automation appears under **Automation**. After your next Apple Pay purchase with the selected card, Qalta will offer to save the expense.

     ![Finished automation in the list](https://qalta.app/assets/apple-pay-ios-26/en/13-automation-list.png)
     *All set*

# Create a Qalta expense with Back Tap

Use Back Tap to launch a Qalta expense shortcut with three taps on the back of your iPhone.

[Add Back tap expense to Shortcuts](https://www.icloud.com/shortcuts/876c51a66dd1491ea01d86fa92e8247a)

## Set up Triple Tap

1.  Open the link above on your iPhone and tap **Add Shortcut** in Shortcuts. It will appear as **Back tap expense**.

2.  Open **Settings → Accessibility → Touch → Back Tap**.

3.  Tap **Triple Tap**, scroll to **Shortcuts**, then select **Back tap expense**.

4.  Now triple-tap the back of your iPhone. The shortcut asks for an amount and category, then creates the expense in **Qalta**.

**You need Qalta.** When it runs, the shortcut asks for the amount and expense category before creating an expense. Make sure Qalta is installed.

[All tutorials](https://qalta.app/tutorials/)

---

# MCP

Connect an AI assistant to your Qalta cloud space.

## Connect an AI assistant

1.  Sign in to Qalta and check that the cloud space you want to use is syncing. Private spaces stored only on your device are not available to the connector.
2.  In your assistant’s settings, add the MCP server https://mcp.qalta.app/mcp.
3.  Sign in through Qalta and review the permissions before approving access.
4.  Start with a read request, such as “How much did I spend on groceries this month?”

# Privacy Policy

Effective date: 16 October 2026

This policy applies to the Qalta mobile app (“the app”) provided by Daniel Tokkozhin (“we”). It explains what stays on your device, what leaves the device, and which companies process that data.

## Private spaces stay on your device

Your records are kept in spaces. A private space, with its accounts, transactions, categories, budgets, goals, debts, recurring items, and similar data, is stored only on your device (SQLite). We do not upload private spaces to our servers.

If you use the optional backup feature, copies can be stored in your iCloud account. That storage is provided by Apple and is covered by Apple’s privacy policy.

## Shared spaces

Sharing is optional. If you share a space, that space and everything in it (its name, accounts, transactions, transfers, categories, budgets, goals, debts, recurring items, and the notes you add) is uploaded to our backend provider, Supabase, and kept in sync with your other devices and with the people you invite. Only members of the space can access it. Each record shows which member created it and who edited it last.

Members of a shared space can see each other’s name, email address, and profile picture from the sign-in account, and when each member joined. Invitations are one-time links that expire after 7 days. We store only a hashed form of the invitation code, and expired invitations are deleted automatically.

When the owner stops sharing or deletes a shared space, its data is deleted from our servers and every member loses access; a copy stays on each member’s device until they remove it. When a member leaves or is removed, they lose access to the data on our servers. If your subscription ends, syncing pauses, and the data already uploaded stays on our servers until the space is deleted.

## Account

You sign in with Sign in with Apple or Sign in with Google. We receive an identity token from Apple or Google and create an account with our backend provider, Supabase. That account can include a user ID, an email address (including Apple’s Hide My Email relay), your name, and, with Google, your profile picture. You can change the name shown to other members in the app.

You can delete your account in the app. That removes the account and subscription records we store. If you own shared spaces with other members, you need to delete those spaces or remove their members first. Data in private spaces on the device is separate; you can also clear local financial data in Settings.

## Subscriptions and purchases

Purchases are processed by Apple. We use RevenueCat to read subscription status. We store a premium flag and AI usage counters (how many voice, image, and document requests you have used) in Supabase, linked to your user ID. We do not receive or store payment card numbers.

## Voice, scan, documents, and other AI features

When you use voice input, receipt or document scan, or other AI extraction, the app sends the content you submitted to our backend (Supabase Edge Functions). The backend forwards that content to OpenAI so the app can propose transactions.

Depending on the feature, that content may include:

-   voice audio;
-   photos of receipts, bills, statements, or similar documents;
-   text extracted from documents;
-   text you typed;
-   names of accounts and categories on the device, plus related amounts and currency, so the model can match them.

This is sent only to provide the feature you asked for. We do not store the submitted content in our database. The backend uses the request to return structured entries and to count usage against your limits.

OpenAI processes the request under its API terms. OpenAI states that, by default, API inputs are not used to train its models. OpenAI may retain data for a limited period to operate the API and for abuse monitoring. See OpenAI’s policies linked below.

AI features are optional. You can add transactions manually without sending this content.

## Analytics, crashes, and other network data

-   **Exchange rates.** The app downloads public currency-rate snapshots from our servers. This is not your journal.
-   **Product analytics (PostHog).** We record events such as which features you use, approximate usage counts (for example, number of transactions, not amounts), and app language. Events are associated with your user ID. We do not send transaction amounts, notes, photos, or audio to PostHog.
-   **Crash reports (Sentry).** We send crash diagnostics to help fix bugs. We do not attach screenshots or extra personal information to those reports.
-   **Technical data.** When the app talks to a server or SDK, that party typically receives technical information such as IP address, device type, and operating system version.

## What we do not do

-   We do not sell your data.
-   We do not use your data for advertising networks or to track you across other companies’ apps and websites.
-   We do not collect precise GPS location. The app uses language and region settings from the device, not GPS.

## Third-party processors

These companies process data as described above. Each has its own privacy policy:

-   [Apple](https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/) — Sign in with Apple, App Store, in-app purchases, optional iCloud backup
-   [Google](https://policies.google.com/privacy) — Sign in with Google
-   [Supabase](https://supabase.com/privacy) — account, subscription and usage records, shared spaces, backend functions
-   [OpenAI](https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy/) — AI processing of content you submit ([API / enterprise privacy](https://openai.com/enterprise-privacy/))
-   [RevenueCat](https://www.revenuecat.com/privacy) — subscription status
-   [PostHog](https://posthog.com/privacy) — product analytics
-   [Sentry](https://sentry.io/privacy/) — crash reports
-   [Expo](https://expo.dev/privacy) — app runtime

We may also disclose information if required by law, or if we believe in good faith that disclosure is needed to protect rights, safety, or to investigate fraud.

## Retention and deletion

-   Data in private spaces remains on your device until you delete it or uninstall the app (unless you also keep an iCloud backup).
-   Data in shared spaces is kept on our servers while the space is shared and is deleted when the owner stops sharing or deletes it.
-   Account and usage records are kept while you have an account, then deleted when you delete the account, plus a short period needed to complete deletion.
-   AI request payloads are processed to fulfill the request. We do not store them as your records. Processors may retain them according to their own policies.
-   Analytics and crash data are kept as needed to operate and improve the app.

To delete account data, use Delete account in the app or email [help.qalta.app@outlook.com](mailto:help.qalta.app@outlook.com).

## Changes

We may update this policy. The effective date above will change. Continued use after an update means you accept the revised policy.

## Contact

Daniel Tokkozhin
[help.qalta.app@outlook.com](mailto:help.qalta.app@outlook.com)

# Terms & Conditions

Effective date: 16 October 2026

These terms apply to the Qalta mobile app (“the app”) provided by Daniel Tokkozhin (“we”). By downloading or using the app, you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, do not use the app.

How we handle data is described in the [Privacy Policy](https://qalta.app/privacy-policy).

## The app

Qalta is a personal expense tracker. You can keep accounts, transactions, budgets, and similar records on your device, and optionally share a space with other people. Some features, including voice input, receipt and document scan, exchange rates, sign-in, shared spaces, and subscriptions, need an internet connection.

The app is provided as a freemium service: core tracking is available without a paid subscription; some features, limits, or AI usage may require a paid plan.

## Your account and your records

You sign in with Sign in with Apple or Sign in with Google. You are responsible for the device you use and for the records you enter. Private spaces are stored on your device, not on our servers. Optional backups, if you enable them, are stored in your iCloud account under Apple’s terms.

You can delete your account in the app. That removes the account and subscription records we store. If you own shared spaces with other members, delete those spaces or remove their members first. Clearing local financial data, or uninstalling the app, is separate from deleting the account.

## Shared spaces

Shared spaces require an active paid subscription. When you share a space, its data is stored on our servers and synced to every member. Every member can view, add, change, and delete records in that space, and those changes reach everyone. Invite only people you trust, and do not upload data you are not allowed to share.

The owner can remove members, stop sharing, or delete the space. Stopping sharing or deleting the space removes its data from our servers for all members; each member keeps a copy on their own device. A space that has stopped sharing cannot be shared again. If your subscription ends, syncing pauses until you renew. We are not responsible for changes other members make to a shared space.

## Subscriptions and purchases

Paid subscriptions and in-app purchases are sold through the Apple App Store and billed by Apple. Prices, billing periods, free trials, and auto-renewal are shown in the app and on the App Store before you buy.

Those purchases are also subject to [Apple’s Licensed Application End User License Agreement](https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/dev/stdeula/). Manage, cancel, or request a refund through your Apple account and Apple’s support, not through us. We do not receive or store payment card numbers.

We may change what a paid plan includes. If we do, we will describe it in the app or on the App Store. We do not guarantee that any particular feature will stay free or paid forever.

## AI features

Voice, scan, and other AI features send the content you submit to our processors so the app can propose transactions. Those suggestions can be wrong or incomplete. You should review them before saving. You can add transactions manually without using AI.

You must not use AI features to submit content you are not allowed to share, or to try to disrupt the service.

## Acceptable use

You may use the app only for lawful personal expense tracking. You may not copy, reverse engineer, or redistribute the app except as allowed by law; misuse AI or other network features; or interfere with the service or other users.

Do not jailbreak or root the device you use for the app. That can make the app unsafe or unusable, and we are not responsible for problems that follow.

## Intellectual property

The app, including its name, design, and code, belongs to us or our licensors. Your records remain yours, including the records you add to shared spaces.

## Updates and ending the service

We may update the app. To keep using it, you may need to install updates and a supported OS version. We do not guarantee that the app will remain available, free, or compatible with every device forever.

We may stop offering the app. If we do, the license to use it ends, and you should stop using it and may delete it from your device. Shared spaces stop syncing. Local records on your device remain until you delete them or uninstall the app, unless you also keep an iCloud backup.

To the extent allowed by law, we are not liable for lost data, incorrect records, subscription or App Store billing disputes handled by Apple, or any indirect or consequential loss from using the app.
